thread:
maria: Hey SRE — support ticket from Acme: their requests to /v1/generate are returning 502/504 intermittently since 12:06pm PST. They report timeouts and increased error rate. SLO alerted: hosted-infer.p99 latency and 5xx fraction.

srebot: [alert] hosted-infer.prod: slo-burn p99 1.6s -> 3.9s, 5xx fraction 7% (threshold 2%). Alert ID: A-48321.

aj: looking. any request IDs from the customer?

maria: they attached two request ids: req_9f3a and req_9f3b. Also included a curl that fails intermittently.

aj: pulling traces for those ids... hmm traces missing for req_9f3a/9f3b — sampling looks low. there's a trace gap around 12:05-12:12.

oliver: i'm seeing a spike of 401s on the auth proxy right before the 5xx spike. query i ran: 
```
logs.query("service:auth-proxy env:prod AND timestamp:[2026-03-17T19:55:00Z TO 2026-03-17T20:20:00Z] | stats count() by status_code")
```
result: 200->normal, 401 increased ~1200 in 5m, then 502/504 downstream.

lee: fwiw, we rolled the billing token rotation job around 12:01pm in prod (automated): billing-service/token-rotate v2.0.2. Could auth cache be holding old tokens?

aj: possible. flow hypothesis: token rotation changed master key -> some auth proxy instances had stale cache -> auth failures -> upstream close or proxy fallback -> 502/504 from gateway. need repro.

maria: support says a quick curl sometimes succeeds, sometimes 502. they included this command:
```
curl -v -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -d '{"input":"hi"}' https://api.redwood.com/v1/generate
```
When we use the new token it succeeds, old token returns 401. But customer claims they were using SDK that caches tokens and didn't refresh.

aj: can we reproduce by forcing the proxy to use stale cached creds? i can spin a canary with 50% old cache TTL to simulate.

oliver: before that, quick mitigation: add a fallback on gateway to bypass auth-proxy caching for a short window (till rotation rollout stabilizes). i'll open a change with tiny window.

aj: creating a query to show timeline correlation:
```
logs.query("service:gateway env:prod AND status:[500 TO 599] AND timestamp:[2026-03-17T19:50:00Z TO 2026-03-17T20:30:00Z] | timeseries count() by status_code")
```
We see 502 spike aligning with auth 401 spike + token-rotate job start.

support-bot: forwarded ticket #ACME-312 to eng-sre with attachments.

lee: note: some edge proxies still running older sidecar image that had a bug where auth cache TTL wasn't invalidated on rotation. that could explain partial success.

aj: plan: (1) short-term: rollback token-rotate rollout to previous stable on remaining hosts OR enable auth bypass fallback; (2) increase trace sampling to 25% for 15m to capture repro; (3) run repro script from a couple regions to validate; (4) postmortem & fix in sidecar to handle rotation gracefully.

maria: can you run the rollback? i can coordinate with support/customer comms.

oliver: rollback started on the remaining 40% of hosts. tagging @oncall-night for continuity.

aj: also instrumented a quick log filter to capture upstream error messages: 
```
logs.query("service:auth-proxy AND message: 'token cache' AND env:prod | tail 200")
```
finding: repeated "cache miss -> fetch token" then "token not found for id" from some pods.

maria: customer confirmed partial improvement after rollback; errors dropped but p99 still elevated.

aj: p99 will normalize once in-flight retries drain. i've bumped sampling to capture any lingering traces. opening issue: INF-5823 (token-rotation resilience).

lee: quick repro steps for devs:
1) helm upgrade token-rotate (canary 100%)
2) run this loop: 
```
for i in {1..200}; do curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $OLD_TOKEN" https://api.redwood.com/v1/generate || echo fail:$i; sleep 0.5; done
```
should see intermittent 401 then downstream 502s on affected proxies.

aj: assigning INF-5823 to oliver, priority P1 for fix in sidecar and robust cache invalidation logic. also adding runbook step to pause rotation if 5xx fraction > 1% during rollout.

maria: thanks. i'll update the customer and close the immediate escalation if errors stay low for next 30m. :thumbsup:

srebot: [note] incident created INF-5823. responders: oliver, aj.

lee: follow-up: we should also add an observability alert that correlates auth 401 spikes with gateway 5xx within 5m window. created ENG-OBS-197.

maria: leaving this thread open for 30m to confirm stability. if anyone repros new issues ping here.

aj: monitoring — p99 trending down, 5xx fraction back to ~0.9%. will report back in 10m.

maria: confirmed with support: customer reports normal now. closing if stable.

aj: closing rollback & adding postmortem template to INF-5823.
